speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, could you please describe your current mental status and any specific symptoms you are experiencing besides the fever?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of fever and altered mentation, reporting fever without chills and rigors. He denies sore throat, abdominal pain, headache, loose stool, burning micturition, or seizures. Has a history of tics and is currently taking haloperidol.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that history. Given your history of tics and current use of haloperidol, I need to rule out Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome, so could you tell me if you have experienced any muscle rigidity, excessive sweating, or tremors recently?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Fever and altered mentation. I also have Profuse sweating, Generalized rigidity, Confusion and disorientation, Ability to move all limbs, Normal deep tendon reflexes with bilateral downgoing plantar responses.

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of fever, altered mentation, generalized rigidity, and profuse sweating in a patient taking haloperidol is highly suggestive of Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome. I will request immediate lab tests to confirm this diagnosis. REQUEST TEST: Creatine_Kinase, Complete_Blood_Count, Comprehensive_Metabolic_Panel

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Creatine Kinase: 5600 U/L (elevated), Complete Blood Count: White Blood Cell Count 14,700/mm3 (elevated), Comprehensive Metabolic Panel: Data not provided

speaker: Doctor
text: The elevated creatine kinase and leukocytosis, combined with your history of haloperidol use, fever, rigidity, and autonomic instability, confirm the diagnosis of Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome. I will proceed with immediate management to stop the offending agent and provide supportive care. DIAGNOSIS READY: Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome
